name: Joi Ito

summary.text: Joichi (Joi) Ito was director of the MIT Media Lab from 2011 until he resigned on September 7, 2019, after reporting on the lab's fundraising from Jeffrey Epstein. MIT's external fact-finding report by Goodwin Procter (January 2020) found Epstein gave $850,000 to MIT between 2002 and 2017, including $525,000 to the Media Lab under Ito, and that Ito and Professor Seth Lloyd, not the central administration, drove the post-conviction gifts. Ito acknowledged in August 2019 that he had also taken $1.2 million from Epstein for his private investment funds. Justice Department releases in 2026 added emails between Ito, Epstein and Reid Hoffman. Ito is now president of the Chiba Institute of Technology.

facts.claim: MIT's external fact-finding report by Goodwin Procter, released January 10, 2020, found that Epstein made 10 gifts to MIT totaling $850,000 between 2002 and 2017, of which $525,000 went to the Media Lab and $225,000 to Professor Seth Lloyd, and that the post-conviction donations were driven by Media Lab director Joi Ito or by Lloyd rather than by MIT's central administration.
facts.quote: Goodwin Procter's fact-finding revealed that between 2002 and 2017, Epstein made 10 separate gifts to MIT, totaling $850,000, of which $525,000 went to the Media Lab and $225,000 to Professor Lloyd.

facts.claim: The Goodwin Procter report found that three MIT vice presidents knew of Epstein's donations and his conviction as early as 2013. MIT Technology Review reported that the report found Ito strategized with Epstein about how to 'mollify the bad press' after articles on a civil suit by Epstein's victims, and Axios reported that the report described a 2013 suggestion by Ito to 'swap donations with someone else's foundation' to conceal the origin of Epstein money.
facts.quote: the report found that three vice presidents knew about both the donations and Epstein's conviction as early as 2013. ... Ito strategized with him as to how he might be able to "mollify the bad press"

facts.claim: The report records that in 2014 Epstein claimed to have arranged an anonymous $2 million donation to the Media Lab from Bill Gates and an anonymous $5 million donation from Leon Black. Goodwin Procter found no evidence that the Gates or Black money was Epstein's; Gates's representatives denied Epstein had anything to do with his donation, and Black's spokesperson said no one from the investigation contacted him.
facts.quote: In 2014, Epstein claimed to have arranged for Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates to provide an anonymous $2 million donation to the Media Lab. He also claimed that same year to have arranged for a $5 million anonymous donation to the Media Lab from Leon Black ... The report found no evidence that the money donated by Gates or Black actually was Epstein's money.

facts.claim: MIT's own records listed Epstein as a 'disqualified donor.' President L. Rafael Reif said the probe found he had signed a letter on August 16, 2012 thanking Epstein for a donation; the final report said Reif was 'not contemporaneously aware of' and 'had no role in approving' MIT's acceptance of the donations.
facts.quote: Reif said the probe found he had signed a letter thanking Epstein, listed as a "disqualified donor" in MIT's own records, for a donation. ... The final report, however, said Reif "was not contemporaneously aware of" and "had no role in approving MIT's acceptance of the donations."

facts.claim: According to the Goodwin Procter report, Epstein visited the MIT campus on July 19, 2013 and met with Media Lab director Joi Ito and Reid Hoffman. The report describes Hoffman as a member of the Media Lab Advisory Council and says that in July 2016 Ito sought Hoffman's advice about whether to allow Epstein to attend a conference, given the concern that attendees would recognize him.
facts.quote: on July 19, 2013, Epstein visited the MIT campus and met with then–Media Lab director Joi Ito and Reid Hoffman. ... in July 2016, Ito sought advice from Reid Hoffman about whether to allow Epstein to attend a conference

facts.claim: On August 15, 2019 Ito publicly apologized for taking Epstein's money, acknowledging $525,000 for the Media Lab and an additional $1.2 million for his private investment funds. On September 6, 2019 The New Yorker reported that the lab's fundraising relationship with Epstein was more extensive than acknowledged and that the lab received at least $7.5 million from other donors channeled through Epstein.
facts.quote: Before the resignation, Ito admitted to having taken $525,000 from Epstein for the Media Lab and an additional $1.2 million for his private ventures. The New Yorker alleged the lab received at least $7.5 million from other donors, channeled through Epstein

Joi Ito, director of MIT Media Lab, resigns over ties to Jeffrey Epstein

facts.claim: Ito resigned as director of the MIT Media Lab and as an MIT professor on September 7, 2019, the day after The New Yorker's report. His email to the provost said it was 'best that I resign as director of the media lab and as a professor and employee of the Institute, effective immediately.' MIT President Reif called the new details 'deeply disturbing' and asked the general counsel to hire a law firm for an independent investigation. Ito also left the board of The New York Times Company that day.
facts.quote: "that it is best that I resign as director of the media lab and as a professor and employee of the Institute, effective immediately." ... Reif also called the new details "deeply disturbing" and asked MIT's general counsel to hire a prominent law firm for an independent investigation.

facts.claim: The Tech reported in February 2026 that newly released Justice Department emails show Epstein helped coordinate the $5 million gift to MIT from Leon Black, which had not been previously reported, and that the emails appear to contradict Bill Gates's account that Epstein had nothing to do with his donations to MIT.
facts.quote: Epstein helped coordinate a $5 million dollar gift to the Institute from Apollo Global Management co-founder Leon Black, which has not been previously reported ... the new emails appear to contradict Bill Gates's account that Jeffrey Epstein had nothing to do with his donations to MIT.

facts.claim: NBC News reported that the 2026 Justice Department release includes a July 2013 message in which Epstein asked Ito about the jail; Ito replied that he had talked to Hoffman about it and that Hoffman 'doesn't judge people.' NBC also reported a November 28, 2018 email in which Ito discussed a trip with Epstein and arranging car pickups for people traveling with him.
facts.quote: In a July 2013 message to Joi Ito, then director of MIT's Media Lab, Epstein asked about the jail; Ito replied that he had talked to Hoffman about it and that he doesn't judge people. ... On November 28, 2018, former MIT Media Lab director Joi Ito sent an email discussing a trip with Epstein.

sources.title: Latest Epstein files release rattles Silicon Valley

facts.claim: In a March 3, 2026 statement on his website, Ito expressed regret for distress caused by commentary on his communications with Epstein released by the Justice Department, pointed to the Goodwin Procter review, and said much recent coverage contained factual errors, including claims that Epstein was a 'disqualified' donor ineligible to give. The Boston Globe reported that Ito said he never witnessed or became aware of evidence of the 'horrific conduct that has since come to light,' and that he would not seek reappointment to a Japanese government technology project.
facts.quote: Much of recent media coverage has contained factual errors. For example, reports and online commentary allege that Epstein was a 'disqualified' donor ineligible to give... The Goodwin Procter report makes clear that these claims are inconsistent with objective facts.

openQuestions: The July 2016 Hoffman-advice passage and the Advisory Council description are quoted from the report by NLPC, an advocacy group; verify the page in the Goodwin Procter PDF.

The New Yorker's $7.5 million figure (September 6, 2019) is cited through TechCrunch and Technology Review because newyorker.com is unreachable; the Goodwin Procter report itself puts Epstein's claimed arranged gifts at $2 million (Gates) plus $5 million (Black).
Counts of Ito-Epstein emails in the 2026 DOJ release vary widely between sources (19 to over 8,000) and were not recorded.
The reported July 2, 2016 Ito email copying Hoffman about 'hiring hackers' appears only on advocacy sites and was left out.
